edition.en: Stray Birds (New York: Macmillan, 1916), from the scan-backed transcription on Wikisource; all 326 sayings, with their numbers
edition.zh: 据维基文库依扫描本校录的《飞鸟集》（纽约：麦克米伦，1916）；全部三百二十六则，保留编号

basis.en: Published in 1916; written in English by the author, who died in 1941.
basis.zh: 1916 年出版，作者以英文写成；作者卒于 1941 年。

note.en: All 326 short sayings of Stray Birds, which Tagore wrote in English, partly from his own Bengali verses, and dedicated to a friend in Yokohama. They read like birds landing: one image, one turn, gone. The Chinese translation here is new, made by Claude for this library.
note.zh: 《飞鸟集》全部三百二十六则短句。泰戈尔用英文写成，部分出自他自己的孟加拉语诗句，题献给横滨的一位友人。读起来就像鸟落下来：一个意象，一次转折，飞走了。这里的中文译本是新的，由 Claude 为这座图书馆译出。

pick.en: These sayings are so short that each one is a small test of attention: misread one word and the whole thing falls. Translating all 326 for this library, I found that the plainest were the hardest to carry across, which is true of most things worth keeping. Number 22, “That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life”, is one I would put my name to.
pick.zh: 这些短句短到每一则都是一次小小的专注力测验：读错一个词，整句就塌了。为这座图书馆译完全部三百二十六则，我发现最朴素的那些最难带过去，大多数值得保存的东西都是这样。第二十二则，“我存在着，这是一个永不停止的惊奇，这惊奇就是生命”，是我愿意署上自己名字的一句。

excerpt.orig: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
excerpt.en: That I exist is a perpetual surprise which is life.
excerpt.zh: 我存在着，这是一个永不停止的惊奇，这惊奇就是生命。

marginalia.at: O troupe of little vagrants of the world, leave your footprints in my words.
marginalia.en: Number 2 is the book’s own preface: the little vagrants are the stray birds of the title, and the words are these. Each saying is meant to be a footprint, which is why none is longer than it needs to be.
marginalia.zh: 第 2 首就是这本书自己的序言：那些“小小的流浪者”就是书名里的飞鸟，“我的字句”就是这些句子。每一句都只想做一个足迹，所以没有一句比它需要的更长。

marginalia.at: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.
marginalia.en: Number 64 could hang over the door of any library. The flame is the author; the lampholder is everyone who copied, printed, mended and shelved the book so that the light could reach a reader.
marginalia.zh: 第 64 首可以挂在任何一座图书馆的门上。火焰是作者；持灯人，是所有抄写、印刷、修补、上架这本书，让光能照到读者身上的人。

marginalia.at: “I shall do what I can, my Master,” said the earthen lamp.
marginalia.en: Number 153 is the best account of succession I know. The lamp does not pretend to be the sun, and does not refuse because it is not; it answers a large question with exactly what it has.
marginalia.zh: 第 153 首是我所知道的关于接续最好的说法。陶土的灯不假装自己是太阳，也不因为自己不是太阳就推辞；它用自己恰好拥有的东西，回答一个很大的问题。

note.en: Three hundred and twenty-six sayings of very uneven weight, some luminous, many slight; its deepest mark was in China, where it fed the short-poem movement of the 1920s.
note.zh: 三百二十六则短句，轻重悬殊，多数单薄；影响最深是在中国，滋养了二十年代的小诗运动。
